sourcedFrom: North American Arms Mini Revolvers — Operation and Safety Manual — ABSENT — no revision or part code printed anywhere in the document (UNDATED — no copyright year is printed anywhere in the document)
cleanIntro: NAA publishes exactly one disassembly for the Black Widow: the cylinder comes out, and nothing else does. That procedure and the cleaning the manual asks for are below, in NAA's own words with the page they sit on.

steps.title: Hammer to half-cock, and know what half-cock is not
steps.action: Place the hammer in the half-cock position — the first hammer stop. Keep every finger behind the muzzle and away from the cylinder-barrel gap while you do it.
steps.prose: NAA is explicit that half-cock is a loading aid and not a safety. The gun's carry safety is the milled slot between chambers, not this notch.
steps.quote: To remove the cylinder, first place the hammer in the half-cock position.
steps.cite: North American Arms Mini Revolvers — Operation and Safety Manual — ABSENT — no revision or part code printed anywhere in the document — LOADING — MINI-MASTER, BLACK WIDOW, PUG, p.6
steps.warn: The traditional half-cock (first hammer stop) position is not intended to serve as a safety

steps.title: Never work on it with a round under the hammer
steps.action: Before anything moves, make sure the hammer is not resting above a live cartridge. NAA states the handgun may discharge if it is dropped or struck on the hammer with a live round underneath, or if your thumb slips while cocking or uncocking with the trigger depressed.
steps.prose: This is the single most dangerous moment on a mini-revolver, and it is the reason the safety slot exists at all.
steps.caution: All fingers must be kept behind the muzzle and away from the cylinder-barrel gap.
steps.quote: Do not carry this handgun with the hammer resting above a live cartridge or in the half-cock position.
steps.cite: North American Arms Mini Revolvers — Operation and Safety Manual — ABSENT — no revision or part code printed anywhere in the document — DANGER, p.5

steps.title: Pull the cylinder pin block down
steps.action: Pull the cylinder pin block downward. On the Black Widow this block is what captures the cylinder pin — the plain .22 LR / .22 Magnum minis use a knurled pin with a release button instead, and that procedure does not apply here.
steps.prose: Down, not out. The block has to clear its seat before it will turn.
steps.quote: Pull the cylinder pin block down.
steps.cite: North American Arms Mini Revolvers — Operation and Safety Manual — ABSENT — no revision or part code printed anywhere in the document — LOADING — MINI-MASTER, BLACK WIDOW, PUG, p.6

steps.title: Turn the block 90 degrees
steps.action: Rotate the cylinder pin block a quarter turn.
steps.prose: A quarter turn is all it takes, and it is what lines the block up with its exit path. If it will not turn, it has not come far enough down.
steps.quote: Turn the cylinder pin block 90 degrees.
steps.cite: North American Arms Mini Revolvers — Operation and Safety Manual — ABSENT — no revision or part code printed anywhere in the document — LOADING — MINI-MASTER, BLACK WIDOW, PUG, p.6

steps.title: Slide the block out toward the muzzle
steps.action: Slide the cylinder pin block out of the gun in the direction of the muzzle end of the barrel.
steps.prose: Forward, always forward. Nothing on this gun comes out rearward.
steps.quote: Slide the cylinder pin block out of the gun in the direction of the muzzle end of the barrel.
steps.cite: North American Arms Mini Revolvers — Operation and Safety Manual — ABSENT — no revision or part code printed anywhere in the document — LOADING — MINI-MASTER, BLACK WIDOW, PUG, p.6

steps.title: Cylinder out, either side
steps.action: Lift the cylinder out of the frame; it comes out from either side of the gun.
steps.prose: With the pin gone there is nothing holding it. On a gun this small the cylinder is easy to drop, so take it out over the bench.
steps.quote: The cylinder can now be easily removed from either side of the gun.
steps.cite: North American Arms Mini Revolvers — Operation and Safety Manual — ABSENT — no revision or part code printed anywhere in the document — LOADING — MINI-MASTER, BLACK WIDOW, PUG, p.6

steps.title: Push the cases out with the cylinder pin
steps.action: Use the cylinder pin itself to push spent cases out of the chambers.
steps.prose: There is no ejector rod on a mini-revolver. The pin is the extractor, and NAA says so.
steps.quote: After firing, follow the same procedure to unload. Use the cylinder pin for extracting empty cases.
steps.cite: North American Arms Mini Revolvers — Operation and Safety Manual — ABSENT — no revision or part code printed anywhere in the document — LOADING — MINI-MASTER, BLACK WIDOW, PUG, p.6

steps.title: Go no further than this
steps.action: Stop at the cylinder. NAA states that disassembly beyond what loading and unloading require voids the warranty outright, and the manual publishes no procedure past cylinder removal.
steps.prose: This is a bound stated by the maker, not a difficulty rating. Frame, barrel, hammer and lockwork stay assembled.
steps.quote: Disassembly of this handgun beyond that required for loading and unloading will render this warranty null and void.
steps.cite: North American Arms Mini Revolvers — Operation and Safety Manual — ABSENT — no revision or part code printed anywhere in the document — WARRANTY, p.2

steps.title: Never use PMC or Armscor Precision ammunition in it
steps.action: Any .22 WMR ammunition may be used in this Magnum mini-revolver except PMC and Armscor Precision branded .22 ammunition, which NAA states has resulted in out-of-battery discharges. Do not put .22 Long Rifle or .22 Short in a Magnum cylinder either.
steps.prose: An out-of-battery discharge on a gun this size is not a malfunction you shrug off. The prohibition names brands, so check the box, not the calibre.
steps.quote: WARNING! DO NOT USE ANY "PMC" OR "ARMSCOR PRECISION" BRANDED AMMUNITION IN ANY NAA Mini-Revolver!
steps.cite: North American Arms Mini Revolvers — Operation and Safety Manual — ABSENT — no revision or part code printed anywhere in the document — AMMUNITION, p.8
steps.warn: You are additionally cautioned NOT to use any .22 caliber Long Rifle (LR) or Short (S) ammunition in a Magnum (WMR) cylinder.

steps.title: Field strip complete — and check this is your manual
steps.action: Frame with barrel, cylinder, and cylinder pin block. That is the whole strip NAA publishes. The book covers the 1860 Earl, the Hogleg, the 1860 Sheriff, the .22 Magnum, .22 Long Rifle and .22 Short minis, the Mini-Master, the Black Widow and the Pug — and it names three different cylinder-removal procedures among them. If your revolver is not one of those nine, this is not its book: NAA directs the owner of any other model to another manual, and this guide does not cover it.
steps.prose: Three procedures sit on the same two pages, and only one of them is the Black Widow's. If your revolver is not on that list, NAA sends you to its own book.
steps.quote: For any other models, refer to their respective owner's manuals.
steps.cite: North American Arms Mini Revolvers — Operation and Safety Manual — ABSENT — no revision or part code printed anywhere in the document — SAFE OPERATIONS, p.3

deepAbsentReason: North American Arms publishes no disassembly of the Black Widow beyond removing the cylinder, and states that "Disassembly of this handgun beyond that required for loading and unloading will render this warranty null and void" (p.2). Its entire maintenance instruction is one sentence about the bore and chamber. So this listing has NO deep clean — that is the manual's answer, not a gap in ours.

cleaning.name: BORE AND CHAMBERS
tasks: Clean the bore and chambers gently after firing — NAA's word is gently
Coat the bore and chambers with a very light film of oil afterwards
Push spent cases out with the cylinder pin rather than prying at them

cleaning.name: CYLINDER AND FRAME
tasks: With the cylinder out, wipe the cylinder faces, the cylinder pin and the frame window clean
Check the safety slots milled in the cylinder rim are clean and undamaged — they are the gun's carry safety
Wipe the outside down with a lightly oiled cloth; keep oil out of the safety slots and the cylinder-barrel gap

cleaning.name: BEFORE IT GOES BACK TOGETHER
tasks: Reverse the removal to insert the cylinder, making sure the cylinder pin seats firmly against the frame and locks in its groove for proper functioning
Check that the cylinder rotates and locks properly each time the hammer is cocked

reassembly: With the hammer at half-cock, put the cylinder back into the frame from either side.
Slide the cylinder pin block back in from the muzzle end, turn it 90 degrees and push it up into its groove.
Make sure the cylinder pin seats firmly against the frame and is locked in its groove — NAA states this is required for proper functioning.

Practise the safety-slot procedure unloaded: draw the hammer slowly back past half-cock until the cylinder turns freely, rotate the cylinder so the hammer aligns with a safety slot, then squeeze the trigger fully and lower the hammer into the slot, holding it the whole way.
Confirm the hammer blade is seated in the safety slot and the cylinder does not rotate.
fncheck: Unloaded, cock the hammer through a full cylinder and confirm it rotates and locks each time — NAA's own instruction is to make sure the cylinder is properly rotated to the locked position every time you cock the gun. Then seat the hammer in a safety slot and confirm the cylinder will not turn.
